_readme: HOW TO EDIT THIS FILE (no coding needed):
1. To change a value, edit the number or text after the colon. Keep the quotes around text, and keep the commas.
2. To add a placement, copy one whole preset block (from { to the matching }) , paste it after the last one, add a comma between blocks, and change the values.
3. Each preset has 'settings' (what the form is filled with) and 'spec' (what the report checks the finished file against).
4. When you confirm a spec with the placement, set status to "verified", fill in verifiedDate, and add the source link.
5. A value of null means 'not specified / keep the source file's value'.
Bitrates are in kilobits per second (kbps). 10000 kbps = 10 Mbps. 'minKbps' and 'maxKbps' are the range the report checks; 'bitrateKbps' is the default the form starts with.

'loudness' modes: off (do nothing), lufs (targetDb = integrated LUFS, peakDb = true peak limit), rms (targetDb = average RMS level, peakDb = peak limit). 'noLetterbox': true makes black bars a FAIL in the report. 'noDuplicateFrames': true marks a placement that rejects repeated frames (the check then flags them as problems).
'group' decides where a placement appears in the list: "Main placements" first, then "More placements". The preset with "custom": true is the Custom option, which shows every setting.

'safeZones' (optional): guides drawn over the preview frames. Each has a label, type ('safe' = keep content inside, 'avoid' = keep content out), and x, y, w, h in pixels on a reference frame of refW x refH. Only add zones that are documented by the placement.

"tile" sets how a placement looks in step 2: "title", a short "sub" line, an accent "color", and an optional "logo" (path to an image in the logos folder, for example "logos/cineplex.svg"). With no logo, the title is shown in the accent colour.

strictness._note: How the report decides PASS / WARN / FAIL. Loudness within loudnessPassDb of target = PASS, within loudnessWarnDb = WARN, else FAIL. A frame counts as a duplicate when its average brightness differs from the previous frame by less than dupDiffThreshold (0 to 255 scale).

limits._note: Browser memory guard. Based on ONE test point (a 526 MB ProRes output worked, using about 2.3 GB of browser memory). Adjust after more testing.

presets.name: Cineplex: cinema pre-show

source.label: Cineplex Media Digital Pre-Show specs, May 2024 (PDF supplied by team; link not yet added)

notes: Audio: the written rule is used (average no higher than -12 dB, peaks no higher than -8 dB). The '-10db' in the spec table is not treated as a target.
The PDF says 8-bit, but ProRes 422 HQ is normally 10-bit. Confirm with Cineplex. This preset uses standard 10-bit ProRes 422 HQ.
File names: max 12 characters, no special characters, end with a language letter (E = English, F = French), for example NAMEE.MOV. Type the name yourself.
Text-safe area is 1724 x 972. Video files only, no stills.

naming.note: Max 12 characters before the extension, letters and numbers only, end with a language letter.

loudness.note: Cineplex sets limits, not a target: average no higher than -12 dB, peaks no higher than -8 dB. Quieter audio is left as it is; louder audio is turned down.

presets.name: Rogers: connected TV (PLACEHOLDER)

source.label: NO PUBLIC SPECS FOUND. Copied from the Bell Media connected TV values until the Rogers Sports & Media rep supplies the real spec.

notes: PLACEHOLDER ONLY. These are Bell Media values, not Rogers values. Replace them when the Rogers spec arrives.

loudness.note: Unknown for Rogers. Uses the common broadcast target of -24 LKFS until confirmed.

presets.name: Crave / Bell Media: connected TV

tile.title: Crave / Bell
tile.sub: Connected TV: Crave, CTV, Noovo, TSN

source.label: Bell Media Digital Advertising Standards and Creative Specifications, April 16 2026, page 15 (Connected TV, VAST)

notes: One spec covers Crave, CTV, Noovo, TSN, CP24, BNN and CTV News on connected TV ("Crave now includes CTV and Noovo").
MP4, H.264, progressive, 1920 x 1080 recommended (1280 x 720 minimum), 16:9. 6, 15 or 30 seconds.
Max file size 25 MB, minimum 5,000 kbps. A 30 s spot must stay near 6 Mbps to fit, so this preset uses a constant 5,800 kbps (constant, so simple scenes do not drop under the minimum).
Frame rates 23.98, 29.97 or 59.94. Bell converts 23.98 to 29.97 on its side.
Audio AAC 44.1 kHz, -24 LKFS (plus or minus 2), average about -12 dB with nothing peaking over -9 dB.

loudness.note: -24 LKFS with peaks held under -9 dB, per the Bell spec.

presets.name: Corus: online video and connected TV

tile.title: Corus
tile.sub: Pre-roll and CTV: StackTV, Pluto TV

source.label: Corus Digital Creative Specifications (PDF supplied by team), In-Stream, Pre-Roll and Connected TV video column

notes: Covers in-stream, pre-roll and connected TV (StackTV, Pluto TV). MP4 only: no MOV on Pluto TV.
MP4, H.264 with AAC audio, 1920 x 1080 recommended (1280 x 720 and 640 x 360 also accepted), 16:9.
29.97 frames per second. A 23.976 video is converted to 29.97 by this preset.
Video bitrate 4,500 to 8,000 kbps; this preset uses a constant 6,000 kbps. Max file 510 MB. 6, 15 or 30 seconds.
Audio AAC 128 kbps, 48 kHz, stereo. The sheet gives no loudness target, so the sound is left as it is.
Send to Corus 5 business days before launch (10 if a third-party vendor is involved).

loudness.note: No loudness rule in the Corus spec sheet.

presets.name: Amazon Prime Video

source.label: Team notes. Link not yet added.

notes: Minimum 15 Mbps video; 50 Mbps recommended for Prime Video. This preset targets 25 Mbps. Raise it if the placement asks for more, but watch the 500 MB limit.
Constant frame rate. Audio minimum 192 kbps.

presets.name: Disney+

source.label: Disney Ad Sales US media kit (via team notes). Canadian requirements not yet checked. Disney+ ANZ 2026 spec and 2025 decline reasons also checked.

notes: Disney's own rejection list says 'duplicate frames' means the file was converted to a different frame rate. The fix is a native-frame-rate export, not grain. Keep the frame rate native.
Constant frame rate, native, no pulldown, progressive. No letterboxing or pillarboxing on 16:9 content. No slates or countdowns. One video track and one audio track.
Keep important content out of the top-right 220 x 135 px (player ad overlay).
Max file size: 250 MB if Hulu-served, 1.9 GB for partner or programmatic. This preset checks 1900 MB. Change it if needed.
Uses H.264 High profile 4:2:0, as in the Disney ANZ 2026 spec. An older note mentioned "Main profile 4:2:2"; confirm with Disney if a file is declined for this.

loudness.note: No target known. Phase 2: type one in.

safeZones.label: Player ad overlay, keep clear (220 x 135)

presets.name: Disney+ (ProRes MOV version)

source.label: Disney Ad Sales US media kit (via team notes). Canadian requirements not yet checked.

notes: Same rules as Disney+ (H.264) but delivered as ProRes 422 HQ in a MOV. Files are large: check the size estimate before encoding.

safeZones.label: Player ad overlay, keep clear (220 x 135)

presets.name: Cineplex: lobby screens (no audio)

source.label: Team notes. Link not yet added.

notes: 1920 x 1080. No audio plays in the lobby. If a client has both contracts, the Pre-Show file can serve both.

naming.note: Assumed to follow the Pre-Show naming rule. Confirm.

presets.name: Landmark Cinemas: pre-show

source.label: Landmark Cinemas Onscreen Advertising Specs & Delivery (2023 rate card PDF, supplied by team)

notes: Digital motion ads: MP4, H.264, 50 Mbps or higher, 24 or 23.976 fps, 1920 x 1080. This preset uses a constant 55 Mbps so simple scenes do not drop under the minimum.

Audio: the spec asks for uncompressed 48 kHz 16-bit WAV or AIFF, the same length as the spot. This preset puts high-quality AAC (320 kbps) inside the MP4. Ask Production@LandmarkCinemas.com whether they also want the sound as a separate WAV.
Audio level: the sheet says average 'higher than -12' with peaks not over -8. Read as the same limits as Cineplex (average no higher than -12 dB, peaks no higher than -8 dB). Confirm with Landmark.
File name must follow LC-Client-SpotName-Duration-Language-Month, for example LC-CAA-TravelInsurance-30-ENG-Dec. Type it yourself.
Text-safe area is 1724 x 972. Deliver through Landmark's WeTransfer page (landmarkcinemas.wetransfer.com).
Showtime slides (2048 x 858 scope and 1998 x 1080 flat JPEGs) are still images, not covered by this tool.

naming.note: Use LC-Client-SpotName-Duration-Language-Month, for example LC-CAA-TravelInsurance-30-ENG-Dec. No spaces.

loudness.note: Landmark sets limits: average no higher than -12 dB, peaks no higher than -8 dB. Quieter audio is left as it is; louder audio is turned down.

presets.name: Spotify video ad

source.label: Team notes. Link not yet added.

notes: 30 seconds or less, max 500 MB, 9:16 or 16:9, at least about 720 x 1280. Audio is required (no silent files).
Loudness: RMS -14 dBFS with peak -0.2 dBFS (Phase 2). RMS is not the same as LUFS; the tool will label which it measures.
Resolution is left as the source's. Vertical files must be supplied by the creative team; this tool does not reframe.

presets.name: YouTube

source.label: Team notes (YouTube recommended upload settings). Link not yet added.

notes: MP4, no edit lists, moov atom at the front, H.264 High, progressive, 2 consecutive B-frames, closed GOP at half the frame rate, 4:2:0, BT.709, VBR, same frame rate as the source.
1080p about 8 Mbps (12 Mbps for 48 to 60 fps). Audio AAC-LC stereo 48 kHz at 384 kbps.
This tool does not deinterlace. Interlaced sources show a warning.
YouTube recommends about 8 to 16 Mbps for 1080p but accepts higher, so no upper limit is checked.
YouTube recommends 384 kbps stereo audio but accepts less, so audio bitrate is not checked. (The encoder delivers less than requested on quiet audio.)

presets.name: YouTube Shorts (vertical, unverified)

source.label: Third-party summaries. Not confirmed. Unknown whether organic Shorts or Shorts ad placements are needed; ad specs may differ.

notes: 9:16, 1080 x 1920, MP4 or MOV, up to 3 minutes. Keep key content inside a centred 4:5 area.
The vertical file must come from the creative team; this tool does not reframe.

presets.name: Meta Reels / Stories (vertical, unverified)

source.label: Third-party summaries. Verify against Meta's own ad specs. Safe zones not yet documented here.

notes: MP4 or MOV, H.264, max 4 GB. 9:16 at 1080 x 1920 with a 720 px minimum short edge. Reels ads up to 90 seconds, Stories up to 120 seconds.
This preset checks the stricter 90 seconds. Change maxDurationSec to 120 for Stories.
The vertical file must come from the creative team; this tool does not reframe.

presets.name: General purpose MP4 (any other placement)

source.label: Generic values accepted by most ad platforms. Not a specific platform spec.

notes: Starting point for any placement not listed. Edit any value to match the spec sheet you were given.

loudness.note: Choose a loudness mode under Loudness if the spec asks for one. Quick picks are provided.

presets.name: Custom (choose the settings yourself)

source.label: Your own settings. Check them against the spec sheet you were given.

notes: Starts from general-purpose MP4 values. Change anything below.

loudness.note: Choose a loudness mode under Loudness if the spec asks for one. Quick picks are provided.

grain._note: Light grain (temporal noise) that stops exact duplicate frames. OFF by default; the page offers it when the frame rate is changed or the check finds repeated frames. Tested 2026-11-09: strength 1 changes nothing, 3 and 5 are unreliable, 4 removed every exact repeat at 6 to 20 Mbps H.264 and ProRes. Use even numbers. A preset can override with "noise": {"strength": 6}.

files._note: Placements with the same "file" value get ONE shared file, made with the "settingsFrom" preset's settings (plus any "settings" here) and checked against the strictest rule of each placement. Remove a placement's "file" line to always give it its own file.

streaming.label: Streaming and online (MP4, high quality)
notes: Audio is 320 kbps so it also meets YouTube's recommendation.

ctv.label: Connected TV, small file (MP4, under 25 MB)
